hypothesis: Channel-steepness steps (dz/dchi two-segment step, 10 m 3DEP) that recur at the same strike across >= 3 independent drainages mark faults, and channels crossing withheld fault segments show larger steps than random same-orientation lines.
mechanism: A fault offsets base level; the steepness contrast propagates upstream as a knickpoint (Kirby & Whipple 2012, J. Struct. Geol. 44, 54-75; Perron & Royden 2013, ESPL 38, 570-576; Gailleton et al. 2019, ESurf 7, 211-230) and persists after the scarp degrades.
mimicking_non_fault_process: Lithologic contacts (resistant-over-weak bedrock), migrating transient knickpoints detached from their source, channel heads / colluvial-fluvial transitions near the A_ch=2e5 m^2 threshold, and playa/pluvial-shoreline base levels. MEASURED: the lane's support is barely enriched near mapped faults (share within 300 m / share of footprint = 1.19 for steps >= ln2, 1.04 for knickpoints), and step-defined channels sit lower in the local relief (median -16 m vs a 20 km median) than the catalogue (median +7 m), so the steps are dominated by these non-fault processes.
